title: Five Bright Planets to Spot in November
summary:
November is a great month for watching planets. You can see them in the evening, around midnight, or just before the sun rises.

In the evening, look for Saturn high in the southern sky. Around midnight, Mars and Jupiter rise in the east-northeast. Early in the month, Mars moves toward Jupiter, passes it on November 16, and then moves away.

Venus is the star of the early morning sky. On November 1, it rises 55 minutes before the sun. By the end of the month, it rises nearly three and a half hours before the sun and shines at its brightest.

Mercury joins the morning show in the middle of the month. It is farthest from the sun on November 20. Here is a trick: your fist, held out at arm's length, covers about 10 degrees of sky.

On November 7, a thin crescent moon, Venus, and the blue star Spica bunch together before sunrise.
why_it_matters: Children can try this themselves, looking up at the right time to spot real planets in the sky.

keywords.explanation: A crescent is a thin, curved shape, like the moon looks when only a small part is lit.
Degrees are units used to measure angles, including how much of the sky something covers.
East-northeast is a direction halfway between east and northeast.
At arm's length means holding something as far away as your stretched-out arm can reach.

background_read: Planets shine in the night sky and can be seen at different times: in the evening, around midnight, or just before the sun rises.
Where a planet appears changes through the month, so sky watchers check dates and directions to find each one.
Venus is especially bright in the early morning sky in November, and Mercury joins the morning show in the middle of the month.
Article_Structure: WHO: The five bright planets Saturn, Mars, Jupiter, Venus and Mercury, which sky watchers can spot.
WHAT: Five bright planets can be seen at different times during November.
WHERE: In the evening sky, around midnight, and in the early morning sky before sunrise.
WHY: The planets appear at different times and places in the sky through the month, and Venus shines at its brightest by the end of it.
